title: Dynamic Disks via StorageClass
description:
**SITUATION:**

Earlier, someone had to **hand-register** archive disk before an app could use it. That does not scale when every team needs disks every week. A **StorageClass** is the catalog entry: when a PVC asks for that class, the cluster can **provision** a real disk automatically — no static PV YAML.

Platform has already registered a StorageClass for this lab (you will not create it). Your job is to **request** storage with a PVC that points at that class, mount it in a small helper Pod, and confirm the claim **Binds** without hand-creating a PersistentVolume.

[DevSetu Blog — Volumes, PVs, PVCs, and StorageClasses](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/volumes-pvs-pvcs-storageclasses)

**YOUR TASK:**

1. The full StorageClass name is intentionally not printed in this brief. **List** StorageClasses in the cluster and select the one whose **name ends with your lab namespace** (`$LEARNER_NS`).
2. On that class, read its annotations for **size** and **mount path** — use those values in your YAML (do not guess).
3. Create a **PVC** that uses that class name + size, plus consumer Pod `cache-writer` that mounts at the annotated path.
4. Verify the claim becomes **Bound** (the provisioner created the disk — you did not hand-create a PV).

**SPEC:**

- StorageClass: name **suffix** is your lab namespace (`$LEARNER_NS`). Shape: `…-<your-namespace>`. Find it with `kubectl get sc` / `describe`.
- From that StorageClass, use:
  - `metadata.name` → PVC `storageClassName`
  - annotation `quickbyte.ai/size-hint` → PVC `resources.requests.storage`
  - annotation `quickbyte.ai/mount-path` → Pod volume mount path
- PVC name: `order-cache-pvc`
- Access modes: `["ReadWriteOnce"]`
- Consumer Pod `cache-writer`: image `busybox:1.36`, volume name `cache`, command `sleep 3600`, mount path = the SC annotation

**GOOD PRACTICES:**

- Manifest: `order-cache-pvc-l22.yaml` (PVC + consumer Pod).
- Do **not** create, update, or delete a StorageClass or PersistentVolume in this challenge.
- Do **not** hand-create a PersistentVolume — let the class provision it.
- Work only in your lab namespace for namespaced objects.

hints: Your namespace is in the lab chrome and in $LEARNER_NS — kubectl already defaults there.
kubectl get sc — pick the class whose name ends with $LEARNER_NS, then describe it for size-hint and mount-path.
Wire those annotation values into the PVC and Pod; do not hard-code guessed paths or sizes.
Work only in your lab namespace (not default).
Read SPEC carefully, apply your YAML, then Submit.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Dynamic Disks via StorageClass

A StorageClass is already in the cluster for this lab. Find it by **namespace suffix**,
read its annotated size/mount hints, then create a PVC + consumer Pod. Do not create
or edit the StorageClass.

Docs: [DevSetu Blog — Volumes, PVs, PVCs, and StorageClasses](/play/devops-engineer/kubernetes/read/volumes-pvs-pvcs-storageclasses) · [StorageClasses](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/storage-classes/)

## 1. Find the StorageClass for this lab

```bash
kubectl get sc
# name ends with $LEARNER_NS (e.g. …-ns-admin)
SC="$(kubectl get sc -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}' \
  | grep -E -- "-${LEARNER_NS}$" | head -1)"
echo "SC=$SC"
kubectl describe sc "$SC"
```

## 2. Read size and mount path from annotations

```bash
SIZE="$(kubectl get sc "$SC" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.quickbyte\.ai/size-hint}')"
MOUNT="$(kubectl get sc "$SC" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.quickbyte\.ai/mount-path}')"
echo "storageClassName=$SC size=$SIZE mountPath=$MOUNT"
```

## 3. Solution YAML

Save as `order-cache-pvc-l22.yaml` (substitute the values you found):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: order-cache-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: <size-hint from SC>
  storageClassName: <discovered SC name>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cache-writer
spec:
  containers:
    - name: writer
      image: busybox:1.36
      command: ["sleep", "3600"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: cache
          mountPath: <mount-path from SC>
  volumes:
    - name: cache
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: order-cache-pvc
```

## Declarative

```bash
kubectl apply -f order-cache-pvc-l22.yaml
kubectl get pvc order-cache-pvc
kubectl get pod cache-writer
```

Wait for the PVC to become **Bound** when CSI can provision (Pod must schedule first because of `WaitForFirstConsumer`), then **Submit**.
